title: ARDY: Autoregressive Diffusion with Hybrid Representation for Interactive Human Motion Generation
summary: Generating realistic 3D human motions in real-time within interactive applications is key for animation, simulation, and humanoid robotics. While recent offline motion generation approaches offer precise control via text and kinematic constraints, they lack the inference speed required for interactive settings. Conversely, existing online methods enable real-time synthesis but often sacrifice controllability or struggle with complex text semantics and long-horizon goals due to limited context windows. In this work, we introduce ARDY, a streaming generation framework that bridges this gap by enabling high-fidelity motion generation controllable via online text prompts and flexible kinematic constraints. ARDY employs a hybrid representation that combines explicit root features with a latent body embedding, balancing precise trajectory control with efficient generative learning. We propose a two-stage autoregressive transformer denoiser that features variable history context and supports conditioning on flexible, long-horizon kinematic constraints. By training on a large-scale motion capture dataset and being directly conditioned on text labels and kinematic constraints sampled from ground truth poses, ARDY natively learns controllable generation that supports online prompting and flexible long-horizon goals. Extensive evaluations on the HumanML3D benchmark and the large-scale, high-fidelity Bones Rigplay dataset demonstrate ARDY's high motion quality and constraint adherence, validating the efficacy of our key architectural decisions. Finally, we demonstrate the method's practical versatility through an interactive demo featuring dynamic text control, diverse keyframe pose constraints, path following, and interactive locomotion control via mouse and keyboard. Supplementary video results, code, and model releases can be found at https://research.nvidia.com/labs/sil/projects/ardy/.

AI.tldr: ARDY is a streaming framework for real-time, high-fidelity 3D human motion generation that combines explicit root features with latent body embeddings and uses a two-stage autoregressive transformer denoiser to enable text and kinematic constraint control, bridging the gap between offline precision and online speed.
AI.motivation: Real-time 3D human motion generation is critical for animation, simulation, and humanoid robotics. Offline methods lack the inference speed needed for interactive settings, while online methods sacrifice controllability or struggle with complex text semantics and long-horizon goals due to limited context windows.
AI.method: ARDY employs a hybrid representation combining explicit root features with latent body embeddings, and a two-stage autoregressive transformer denoiser with variable history context. It supports conditioning on flexible, long-horizon kinematic constraints and is trained on large-scale motion capture data conditioned on both text labels and ground truth kinematic constraints.
AI.result: Extensive evaluations on HumanML3D and the Bones Rigplay dataset demonstrate ARDY's high motion quality and constraint adherence. An interactive demo shows practical versatility with dynamic text control, keyframe pose constraints, path following, and mouse/keyboard locomotion control.
AI.conclusion: ARDY effectively bridges the gap between real-time generation speed and precise control capabilities, validating the efficacy of its key architectural decisions for interactive applications requiring text and kinematic constraint control.

title: Collective Intelligence with Foundation Models
comment: Accepted as a book chapter in "Advances in Global Applied Artificial Intelligence" (G. A. Tsihrintzis, M. Virvou, N. G. Bourbakis, L. C. Jain, Eds.), authenticated version will be published in Springer series: Learning and Analytics in Intelligent Systems
summary: As foundation models grow in scale and diversity, coordinating multiple models into cooperative reasoning systems offers a path toward safer, more reliable AI. This chapter presents a multi-agent framework where solver models generate independent drafts, each undergoes structured critique and revision by a critic agent, and an aggregator agent synthesizes a final consensus solution. A scoring module provides semantic, numerical, and procedural evaluation across all agents. Through ablation studies on a benchmark spanning calculus, physics, chemistry, biology, economics, optimization, statistics, and mathematics, we isolate the contributions of framework architecture versus model diversity. We compare four configurations: (1) Individual Baseline, (2) Homogeneous Framework using one shared model, (3) Redundant Homogeneous Solvers using multiple instances of the same model, and (4) Heterogeneous Framework with diverse specialized models. Results show that while framework structure and redundant sampling yield modest gains, model heterogeneity is the critical factor driving substantial performance improvements. The heterogeneous configuration achieves superior step-wise accuracy (0.64 vs. 0.54 for individual models; 2.3x improvement over homogeneous configurations) with reduced variance across categories and difficulty levels. Step-wise reasoning quality (correctness of intermediate steps, not just final answers) improves dramatically only with model diversity, showing that heterogeneous agents provide complementary error detection and reasoning refinement essential for explainability and auditability. We discuss architectural principles, evaluation methodology, and implications for Global Applied AI, showing how heterogeneous multi-agent coordination supports transparent, auditable, high-confidence decision-making across scientific and industrial domains.

AI.tldr: A multi-agent framework for cooperative reasoning systems where diverse models collaborate to generate, critique, and synthesize solutions, demonstrating that model heterogeneity rather than framework structure is the critical factor driving substantial performance improvements in step-wise reasoning accuracy and explainability.
AI.motivation: As foundation models grow in scale and diversity, coordinating multiple models into cooperative reasoning systems offers a path toward safer, more reliable AI.
AI.method: A multi-agent framework where solver models generate independent drafts, critic agents provide structured critique and revision, and an aggregator synthesizes a final consensus solution. A scoring module evaluates across semantic, numerical, and procedural dimensions. Four configurations compared: (1) Individual Baseline, (2) Homogeneous Framework using one shared model, (3) Redundant Homogeneous Solvers using multiple instances of the same model, and (4) Heterogeneous Framework with diverse specialized models.
AI.result: Model heterogeneity is the critical factor for performance improvements. The heterogeneous configuration achieves superior step-wise accuracy (0.64 vs. 0.54 for individual models; 2.3x improvement over homogeneous configurations) with reduced variance across categories and difficulty levels. Step-wise reasoning quality improves dramatically only with model diversity, demonstrating that heterogeneous agents provide complementary error detection and reasoning refinement.
AI.conclusion: Heterogeneous multi-agent coordination supports transparent, auditable, high-confidence decision-making across scientific and industrial domains. The framework demonstrates that model diversity provides complementary error detection and reasoning refinement essential for explainability and auditability, establishing architectural principles for Global Applied AI systems.

title: Time-to-Collision Based Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance Using Pretrained Vision Models for Robots in Unstructured Environments
summary: Dynamic obstacle avoidance in unstructured outdoor environments remains a critical challenge for autonomous mobile robots, particularly when large-scale robot-specific training data and simulation-based policies are impractical. We present a data-efficient, interpretable method for vision-based dynamic obstacle avoidance that operates entirely on real-world data, avoiding the sim-to-real transfer problem inherent in simulation-trained policies. Our approach leverages UniDepth, a large pretrained monocular depth estimation model, to produce dense depth maps from RGB video without requiring stereo cameras or LiDAR at inference time. Dynamic obstacle avoidance is achieved by extending the SuperPoint and SuperGlue feature correspondence pipeline to track keypoints across long frame sequences, projecting their 2D pixel-space positions into 3D using camera intrinsics and predicted depth, running bundle adjustment initialized from these 3D keypoints, and computing per-keypoint time-to-collision (TTC). A 2D motion primitive in the ground plane is then selected to move the robot away from the closest point of approach of the minimum-TTC keypoint. Evaluated on real-world data from the M3ED dataset, our pipeline achieves a precision of 0.49 and a recall of 0.38 in identifying frames with a ground truth TTC below 1 second, and correctly generates the evasive motion direction in 84\% of true positive detections. Crucially, it detects at least one frame with TTC less than 1 second for 20 out of 22 unique physical obstacles present in our test sequences. Unlike end-to-end learned methods that demand thousands of hours of robot-specific training data, our approach eliminates model training entirely, requiring only 74 seconds of data for hyperparameter tuning. This demonstrates exceptional data efficiency while preserving interpretable and generalizable behavior across diverse obstacle types.

AI.tldr: A data-efficient, interpretable vision-based dynamic obstacle avoidance method that uses UniDepth for monocular depth estimation and SuperPoint/SuperGlue for feature tracking, eliminating the need for sim-to-real transfer and requiring minimal training data.
AI.motivation: Dynamic obstacle avoidance in unstructured outdoor environments is challenging due to the impracticality of large-scale robot-specific training data and simulation-based policies, with the sim-to-real transfer problem being inherent in simulation-trained approaches.
AI.method: Uses UniDepth (pretrained monocular depth estimation) to produce dense depth maps from RGB video; extends SuperPoint and SuperGlue feature correspondence pipeline to track keypoints across long frame sequences; projects 2D pixel positions into 3D using camera intrinsics and predicted depth; runs bundle adjustment; computes per-keypoint time-to-collision (TTC); selects a 2D motion primitive based on minimum-TTC keypoint.
AI.result: Achieves precision of 0.49 and recall of 0.38 in identifying frames with TTC below 1 second on M3ED dataset; correctly generates evasive motion direction in 84% of true positive detections; detects at least one frame with TTC less than 1 second for 20 out of 22 unique physical obstacles; requires only 74 seconds of data for hyperparameter tuning.
AI.conclusion: Unlike end-to-end learned methods requiring thousands of hours of robot-specific training data, this approach eliminates model training entirely, demonstrating exceptional data efficiency while preserving interpretable and generalizable behavior across diverse obstacle types.

title: From Triggers to Emotions: A CPM-Grounded Appraisal Multi-Agent for Dynamic Emotional Evolution in Persona-Based Dialogue
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have substantially advanced persona-based dialogue agents for emotion-sensitive role simulation in healthcare, education, counseling, customer service, and interactive storytelling. However, two related lines of work leave a key gap. Persona-based dialogue systems often encode emotions as static traits or surface-level stylistic cues, and affective dialogue research has largely focused on empathetic response generation toward users rather than modeling the agent persona's own evolving emotional state. As a result, trigger-driven emotional evolution within a character remains underexplored. To address this limitation, we draw inspiration from the Component Process Model (CPM), a psychological theory that views emotion as a dynamic process shaped by the appraisal of external events. We propose CPM-MultiAgent, a CPM-grounded emotion evolution multi-agent framework for supporting emotional changes in persona-based dialogue. Instead of treating a character's emotion as a fixed attribute, CPM-MultiAgent represents it as a latent state that is continuously reshaped by dialogue triggers. Through affective trigger extraction, CPM-based collaborative appraisal, and emotion state updating, the framework enables more emotionally consistent role simulation in multi-turn interactions.Experiments with baseline comparisons, ablation studies, human evaluation, and case analyses demonstrate that CPM-MultiAgent effectively models dynamic emotional evolution in emotionally sensitive role-simulation settings.

AI.tldr: A CPM-grounded multi-agent framework that models dynamic emotional evolution in persona-based dialogue systems by representing emotions as latent states continuously reshaped by dialogue triggers through affective trigger extraction, collaborative appraisal, and emotion state updating.
AI.motivation: LLMs have advanced persona-based dialogue agents, but current approaches encode emotions as static traits or surface-level cues and focus on user empathy rather than modeling the agent's own evolving emotional state, leaving trigger-driven emotional evolution within characters underexplored.
AI.method: Inspired by the Component Process Model (CPM) psychological theory, CPM-MultiAgent represents character emotion as a latent state continuously reshaped by dialogue triggers. The framework includes affective trigger extraction, CPM-based collaborative appraisal, and emotion state updating components.
AI.result: Experiments with baseline comparisons, ablation studies, human evaluation, and case analyses demonstrate that CPM-MultiAgent effectively models dynamic emotional evolution and enables more emotionally consistent role simulation in multi-turn interactions.
AI.conclusion: The framework successfully addresses the gap in modeling trigger-driven emotional evolution by providing a psychologically grounded approach to dynamic emotion modeling, showing effectiveness through comprehensive evaluation across multiple metrics and analyses.

title: Monocular Vision Based Control Framework for Grasping
comment: This paper is accepted at IEEE/ASME International Conference on Advanced Intelligent Mechatronics 2026 (AIM 202^)
summary: Grasping in unstructured environments requires handling objects with widely different mechanical properties, from soft and deformable items to rigid everyday objects. Most existing approaches address these categories separately and often rely on tactile sensing, object-specific models, or specialized grippers. In this paper, we present a unified monocular vision-based grasping framework that targets both soft and rigid objects within a single control pipeline, using only RGB input and a position-controlled gripper. The proposed system combines open-vocabulary object detection, image segmentation, boundary-aware point assignment, real-time point tracking, and monocular depth estimation to recover object motion and geometry from visual observations. A key component of the framework is a language-based stiffness estimation model that infers an object's expected compliance from its semantic description and provides an object-level prior for selecting the grasping strategy before contact. For deformable objects, grasp adaptation is governed by a Procrustes-based dissimilarity measure computed from tracked keypoints, which acts as a visual proxy for deformation. For rigid objects, the gripper width is regulated through the scaling of tracked point distances. We validate the proposed method in real-world pick-and-place experiments on a Franka Emika Research 3 arm using objects with substantially different mechanical properties, including lettuce, fresh mozzarella cheese, croissants, paper towels, and hard plastic bottles. Results demonstrate that the framework achieves stable grasping across both soft and rigid objects using visual feedback alone, highlighting a practical, sensor-efficient, and generalizable approach for food handling and household manipulation.

AI.tldr: A unified monocular vision-based grasping framework that handles both soft and rigid objects using only RGB input and a position-controlled gripper, with language-based stiffness estimation and visual tracking.
AI.motivation: Existing approaches address soft and rigid object grasping separately and often rely on tactile sensing, object-specific models, or specialized grippers. There is a need for a unified, sensor-efficient approach that can handle objects with widely different mechanical properties in unstructured environments.
AI.method: The system combines open-vocabulary object detection, image segmentation, boundary-aware point assignment, real-time point tracking, and monocular depth estimation. It includes a language-based stiffness estimation model that infers object compliance from semantic descriptions, a Procrustes-based dissimilarity measure for deformable object grasp adaptation, and scaling of tracked point distances for rigid object gripper width regulation.
AI.result: Validated on a Franka Emika Research 3 arm using lettuce, fresh mozzarella cheese, croissants, paper towels, and hard plastic bottles. The framework achieves stable grasping across both soft and rigid objects using only visual feedback.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method demonstrates a practical, sensor-efficient, and generalizable approach for food handling and household manipulation, eliminating the need for tactile sensing, object-specific models, or specialized grippers.

title: Early to Share, Late to Save: Synchronisation-Driven Communication Gating in Bandwidth-Constrained Cooperative VLN
comment: Accepted at the IJCAI 2026 GLOW Workshop. To appear in Springer Communications in Computer and Information Science (CCIS)
summary: Most cooperative Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) methods assume unlimited communication, not considering real-world applications where bandwidth is restricted and information efficiency is critical. We introduce \textbf{bandwidth-constrained cooperative VLN} and propose \textbf{hindsight gating}: a lightweight supervised gate that labels communication-critical steps post-hoc from navigation failures, avoiding the high variance of REINFORCE. Contrary to the intuition that agents should communicate when uncertain, we observe a consistent counter-intuitive pattern: trained gates fire predominantly in early episode steps and more often when agents are confident, across all budget levels ($B \in \{1,3,5\}$). We explain this through \textbf{recurrent hidden-state alignment}: early communication injects grounded trajectory representations that persist and compound through subsequent Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) updates, achieving $+0.072$ cumulative alignment gain with $B{=}3$ transmissions, approaching unconstrained communication ($+0.078$) at 260\% greater alignment efficiency than random gating ($+0.020$) and 320\% greater efficiency than entropy-based gating ($+0.017$). Our results establish a new communication regime for bandwidth-limited embodied agents: synchronise representations early, navigate independently later. Our codebase is available at: https://github.com/AravG13/bandwidth-constrained-cooperative-vln

AI.tldr: Bandwidth-constrained cooperative VLN introduces hindsight gating, a lightweight post-hoc supervised gate that fires early and when agents are confident to synchronize representations via recurrent hidden-state alignment, achieving 260-320% higher alignment efficiency than random or entropy-based gating.
AI.motivation: Most cooperative VLN methods assume unlimited communication, ignoring real-world bandwidth constraints and information efficiency needs.
AI.method: Hindsight gating: a lightweight supervised gate that labels communication-critical steps post-hoc from navigation failures (avoiding REINFORCE variance). The gate fires in early steps and when agents are confident, explained by recurrent hidden-state alignment where early communication injects grounded trajectory representations that persist through GRU updates.
AI.result: Trained gates fire predominantly in early episode steps and when agents are confident across all budget levels. Achieves +0.072 cumulative alignment gain with B=3 transmissions, approaching unconstrained communication (+0.078) at 260% greater efficiency than random gating and 320% greater efficiency than entropy-based gating.
AI.conclusion: Establishes a new communication regime for bandwidth-limited embodied agents: synchronize representations early, navigate independently later.

title: Towards Soft Robotic Exogloves for Musculoskeletal Manipulation to Reduce Pain and Spasticity
comment: 8 pages, 15 figures. To be published in the IEEE RAS/EMBS 11th International Conference on Biomedical Robotics and Biomechatronics (BioRob 2026)
summary: Hand spasticity and resulting pain affect 12 million people worldwide, including stroke survivors, arthritis patients, and those with other muscle and nerve deficiencies. Soft robotic exogloves are being introduced to help patients enhance mobility or manage pain; however, there are no current solutions that address both pain and mobility. We present preliminary development of a soft robotic exoglove that both aids in mobility and administers massage-like compression to relax spastic muscles. The glove consists of soft pneumatic actuators that are personalized to an individual's hand topology and kinematics, allowing for optimal conformability and targeted mobility. Novel soft actuators were designed, analyzed, fabricated, assembled into an exoglove, and experimentally tested. Actuators were 3D modeled and analyzed with finite element modeling under pressures of 100 and 200 kPa. Geometries were optimized to minimize stress before fabrication and testing. A dorsal finger actuator was successfully customized to a participant's hand topology, providing full conformal contact and maximal force distribution. A ventral finger actuator was successfully fabricated that can be drastically compressed in size to fit into the tight space of a hyperflexed spastic finger. A palmar actuator was successfully printed with stereolithography, showing potential for 3D-printed soft actuators with more complex geometries. The glove was assembled and successfully worn by a pilot user to validate initial findings in comfort and effectiveness.

AI.tldr: A soft robotic exoglove is developed that combines mobility assistance with massage-like compression therapy to address both spasticity and pain simultaneously.
AI.motivation: Hand spasticity and pain affect 12 million people worldwide, yet existing soft robotic exogloves only address mobility or pain separately, with no solution providing both benefits.
AI.method: Novel soft pneumatic actuators were designed, modeled with finite element analysis at 100 and 200 kPa, and fabricated using stereolithography. The glove features dorsal finger actuators customized to individual hand topology for conformal contact, ventral finger actuators capable of drastic compression for hyperflexed spastic fingers, and a palmar actuator printed via stereolithography. The glove was assembled and tested on a pilot user.
AI.result: Successfully fabricated and customized actuators including a dorsal finger actuator with full conformal contact and force distribution, a ventral finger actuator that compresses to fit tight spaces in hyperflexed spastic fingers, and a stereolithography-printed palmar actuator. The glove was successfully worn by a pilot user, validating comfort and effectiveness.
AI.conclusion: The preliminary development demonstrates the feasibility of a soft robotic exoglove that simultaneously addresses both mobility enhancement and pain management through massage-like compression, providing a novel solution for patients with hand spasticity and related pain conditions.

title: Soft Robotic Exogloves for Dexterous Mobility -- Towards Personalized Rehabilitation
comment: 8 pages, 14 figures. To be published in The IEEE RAS/EMBS 11th International Conference on Biomedical Robotics and Biomechatronics (BioRob 2026)
summary: Soft robotic exogloves can provide hand rehabilitation and assistance. Fitting these gloves often relies on standardized measurements not tailored to the individual, limiting their effectiveness, especially for fine articulation necessary for dexterous manipulation. We present the design, fabrication, modeling, and testing of a personalized pneumatically-actuated soft robotic exoglove. The glove was fit to a user's hand with topological scans and fabricated with silicone mold casting. Finite element analysis (FEA) was performed to evaluate actuator bending and forces from physical human-robot interaction (pHRI) between an actuator and a simplified personalized biomechanical finger model. Pneumatic pressure control experiments were conducted to flex the user's finger with static and dynamic references. Fabrication results show that topological scans enable precise tailoring to hand anatomy. Simulations showed that anatomical personalization enables analysis of pHRI contact forces, and results indicate sufficient joint mobilization with non-ideal compression on the proximal phalanx. Pneumatic testing indicates that pressure control allows accurate and targeted mobility of the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) and proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joints with intrinsic stiffness. Testing of multiple designs showed that relaxing the strain-limiting layer improves actuator-to-finger joint alignment during actuation. This work presents personalization to the human hand in structural conformability, joint topology, modeling of pHRI contact, and time-dependent actuation-deformation profiles. This lays a groundwork for informing exoglove design optimization to enable assistance in dexterous manipulation and neuromuscular rehabilitation of fine motor skills.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a personalized pneumatically-actuated soft robotic exoglove for hand rehabilitation and assistance, designed through topological scanning, silicone mold casting, and validated through FEA and pneumatic testing.
AI.motivation: Soft robotic exogloves for hand rehabilitation and assistance often rely on standardized measurements not tailored to individuals, limiting their effectiveness for fine articulation needed in dexterous manipulation.
AI.method: The authors designed and fabricated a personalized pneumatically-actuated soft robotic exoglove by fitting the glove to a user's hand via topological scans and silicone mold casting. They performed finite element analysis (FEA) to evaluate actuator bending and physical human-robot interaction (pHRI) forces between an actuator and a simplified personalized biomechanical finger model. Pneumatic pressure control experiments were conducted with static and dynamic references. Testing of multiple designs explored the effect of relaxing the strain-limiting layer on actuator-to-finger joint alignment.
AI.result: Topological scans enable precise tailoring to hand anatomy. Anatomical personalization allows analysis of pHRI contact forces and achieves sufficient joint mobilization with non-ideal compression on the proximal phalanx. Pneumatic pressure control enables accurate and targeted mobility of the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) and proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joints with intrinsic stiffness. Relaxing the strain-limiting layer improves actuator-to-finger joint alignment during actuation.
AI.conclusion: This work presents personalization in structural conformability, joint topology, modeling of pHRI contact, and time-dependent actuation-deformation profiles. It lays a groundwork for informing exoglove design optimization to enable assistance in dexterous manipulation and neuromuscular rehabilitation of fine motor skills.

title: In vivo feasibility study of humanoid robots in surgery
summary: Recent advances in actuation, control and learning have rapidly pushed humanoid robots from a distant vision towards near-term real-world deployment. Healthcare is a particularly pressing domain, in which staffing shortages and increasing care demand are widening the gap between clinical workload and available skilled labour. Although current automation has largely focused on digital and logistical tasks, much hospital work remains embodied, requiring mobility, manipulation and safe interaction in human-designed environments. Humanoid form factors offer unique potential, particularly for assisting with surgical tasks. Traditionally, robotic systems for surgery are purpose-built platforms such as Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci Surgical System, and it remains unclear how close current humanoid systems are to meeting the precision, control and safety requirements of minimally invasive surgery. Here we present a systematic evaluation of contemporary humanoid technology for laparoscopic surgical tasks. We develop a humanoid-based laparoscopic teleoperation framework using general-purpose instruments and assess its abilities through benchtop characterization, dry-laboratory user studies spanning diverse surgical experience levels and in vivo porcine studies. Across these evaluations, we quantify technical feasibility, task performance and clinical readiness relative to established surgical platforms. Together, our study provides an evidence-based assessment of current humanoid abilities and limitations for surgical applications, highlighting both their promise and key technical challenges that must be addressed before clinical deployment.

AI.tldr: A systematic evaluation of contemporary humanoid technology for laparoscopic surgical tasks, developing a humanoid-based teleoperation framework and assessing its capabilities through benchtop, user, and in vivo studies.
AI.motivation: Healthcare faces staffing shortages and increasing care demand. Current automation focuses on digital/logistical tasks, but hospital work remains embodied, requiring mobility, manipulation, and safe interaction. Humanoid robots could assist with surgical tasks, but it's unclear if current systems meet the precision, control, and safety requirements of minimally invasive surgery.
AI.method: Developed a humanoid-based laparoscopic teleoperation framework using general-purpose instruments. Assessed abilities through three evaluation methods: benchtop characterization, dry-laboratory user studies spanning diverse surgical experience levels, and in vivo porcine studies. Quantified technical feasibility, task performance, and clinical readiness relative to established surgical platforms.
AI.result: The study quantifies technical feasibility, task performance, and clinical readiness across all evaluation methods, providing an evidence-based assessment of current humanoid abilities and limitations for surgical applications.
AI.conclusion: Humanoid robots show promise for surgical applications, but significant technical challenges remain that must be addressed before clinical deployment. The study provides a comprehensive evidence-based assessment to guide future development.

title: D-CLIPSE: Distributed Consensus-based Localization with Passive Listening on Shared State Exchange
comment: 8 pages, 7 figures, 1 table. Submitted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
summary: Multi-robot localization that is accurate and consistent is imperative for downstream tasks such as planning and control. Centralized filtering approaches optimally fuse all available sensor measurements of the team. However, a centralized solution is rarely implementable due to hardware, communication, and computational constraints. Distributed approaches deploy a filter on each robot to estimate their own state and neighbours' states using inter-robot communication. This paper proposes a consistent, communication-efficient, and consensus-based distributed filtering framework that shares both preintegrated odometry and relevant shared states among communicating robots. The proposed method is validated in simulated and experimental scenarios, showing near centralized performance in accuracy, and especially in consistency, compared to the current state-of-the-art decentralized approach.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a consensus-based distributed filtering framework for multi-robot localization that shares preintegrated odometry and shared states among robots, achieving near centralized performance in accuracy and consistency compared to state-of-the-art decentralized approaches.
AI.motivation: Accurate and consistent multi-robot localization is crucial for downstream tasks like planning and control. While centralized filtering optimally fuses all measurements, it's rarely implementable due to hardware, communication, and computational constraints. Existing distributed approaches have limitations that this paper addresses.
AI.method: A consistent, communication-efficient, consensus-based distributed filtering framework that enables robots to share both preintegrated odometry and relevant shared states during inter-robot communication.
AI.result: Validated in simulated and experimental scenarios, the proposed method demonstrates near centralized performance in accuracy, with especially improved consistency compared to the current state-of-the-art decentralized approach.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework achieves near centralized performance while remaining distributed, making it practical for real-world implementation where centralized solutions are infeasible.

title: Factors Influencing Conversational Engagement in Robot-Delivered Individual Cognitive Stimulation Therapy (iCST) for Dementia in Home Settings
comment: Accepted for publication at the IEEE RO-MAN Conference 2026
summary: Social robots offer a promising means of supporting cognitive therapies for dementia care by guiding structured conversation and therapeutic activities. However, little is known about the conversational dynamics that emerge during robot-delivered cognitive stimulation therapy (CST) sessions. This study analysed the interaction patterns from robot-delivered individual CST (iCST) sessions conducted with people living with dementia in home settings. Our Co-STAR (Cognitive Stimulation Therapy by an Autonomous Robot) system was deployed in the homes of eight PwDs for one week, who completed 30-minute sessions. Conversational metrics, including words per turn, speech production rate, response duration, response latency, and self-referential language, were analysed to examine how conversational engagement is shaped by prompt personalisation, interaction phase, and participant characteristics. The findings highlight three key interactional properties of robot-delivered iCST. First, personalised prompts significantly increase response duration, self-referential language, and overall engagement compared to generic prompts. Second, conversational behaviour changes within sessions, with a reduction in the verbal output and autobiographical engagement observed during later interaction phases, which suggests cognitive fatigue. Third, first-session conversational metrics were associated with long-term participation, while living situation influenced conversational engagement patterns. These findings provide empirical insights into the factors that shape conversational engagement in robot-delivered iCST. They inform the design of adaptive conversational robots for dementia therapy.

AI.tldr: This study analyzed conversational dynamics in robot-delivered Cognitive Stimulation Therapy (iCST) for people living with dementia in home settings, using the Co-STAR system with 8 participants over one week.
AI.motivation: Social robots offer promising support for dementia cognitive therapies by guiding structured conversation and activities, but conversational dynamics during robot-delivered cognitive stimulation therapy (CST) sessions are poorly understood.
AI.method: The Co-STAR system was deployed in homes of 8 people living with dementia for 30-minute sessions. Conversational metrics including words per turn, speech production rate, response duration, response latency, and self-referential language were analyzed to examine how engagement is shaped by prompt personalization, interaction phase, and participant characteristics.
AI.result: Three key findings: (1) Personalized prompts significantly increase response duration, self-referential language, and overall engagement; (2) Conversational behavior changes within sessions with reduced verbal output and autobiographical engagement in later phases, suggesting cognitive fatigue; (3) First-session metrics predicted long-term participation, while living situation influenced engagement patterns.
AI.conclusion: These findings provide empirical insights into factors shaping conversational engagement in robot-delivered iCST, informing the design of adaptive conversational robots for dementia therapy.

title: RadLoc: Radar-based 3-DoF Global Localization via Fast, Robust, and Lightweight Spatial Descriptor Across Diverse Environmental Scenarios
summary: While global localization using spinning radar has gained attention for its robustness to adverse weather and challenging environments, many studies have focused on individual components such as place recognition or pose estimation. In this paper, we take a holistic view of radar sensor-based global localization and present RadLoc, a fast, robust, and lightweight end-to-end pipeline from place recognition to 3-DoF pose estimation. RadLoc accelerates pre-processing using 1D CA-CFAR filtering and leverages the near-range dominance in spinning radar images to design a compact descriptor and an efficient hierarchical coarse-to-fine retrieval strategy. Moreover, coupled with phase correlation-based 3-DoF pose estimation, it forms a versatile global localization module applicable to SLAM and multi-session SLAM systems. Extensive experiments on 15 sequences across 5 datasets demonstrate that RadLoc achieves robust performance while maintaining the smallest descriptor size and fastest retrieval time among state-of-the-art approaches. The supplementary materials are available at https://sparolab.github.io/research/radloc/.

AI.tldr: RadLoc is an end-to-end pipeline for radar-based global localization that accelerates preprocessing with 1D CA-CFAR filtering, leverages near-range dominance for compact descriptors, implements hierarchical coarse-to-fine retrieval, and combines phase correlation for 3-DoF pose estimation, achieving robust performance with the smallest descriptor size and fastest retrieval time among state-of-the-art methods.
AI.motivation: Global localization using spinning radar is gaining attention for its robustness to adverse weather and challenging environments, but existing studies focus on individual components (place recognition, pose estimation) rather than a holistic end-to-end pipeline. A fast, robust, and lightweight solution is needed.
AI.method: RadLoc implements a holistic pipeline from place recognition to 3-DoF pose estimation using 1D CA-CFAR filtering for preprocessing acceleration, a compact descriptor based on near-range dominance in radar images, an efficient hierarchical coarse-to-fine retrieval strategy, and phase correlation-based 3-DoF pose estimation.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on 15 sequences across 5 datasets demonstrate RadLoc achieves robust performance while maintaining the smallest descriptor size and fastest retrieval time among state-of-the-art approaches.
AI.conclusion: RadLoc presents a versatile global localization module applicable to SLAM and multi-session SLAM systems, demonstrating that a holistic approach to radar sensor-based localization can outperform individual-component methods in terms of descriptor efficiency and retrieval speed while preserving robustness.

title: X-ACTA: eXtended Analytic Center Tension distribution Algorithm for fixed and mobile cable-driven-parallel-robot
summary: Steering Cable-Driven Parallel Robots (CDPRs) beyond their Wrench-Feasible Workspace (WFW) augments their capabilities in challenging scenarios such as during aggressive maneuvers or following a cable failure. In this context, although the determination of cable tensions is a well-studied topic, only a few approaches address these scenarios. Therefore, this paper introduces an extended version of the Analytic Center method as a criterion for selecting cable tensions outside the WFW while maintaining differentiability and including non-linear constraints. Notably, the proposed method maintains continuous and differentiable tension profiles, ensures fast real-time convergence to a unique solution, and, in contrast to other slack-based formulations, relegates wrench errors to a negligible area of the WFW. Its superiority in terms of smoothness and wrench error is confirmed via Pareto dominance with respect to the leading state-of-the-art method. Lastly, the effectiveness of the method is demonstrated through numerical experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper develops an extended Analytic Center method for determining cable tensions in cable-driven parallel robots (CDPRs) when operating beyond their wrench-feasible workspace (WFW), enabling the robots to handle aggressive maneuvers and cable failure scenarios while maintaining smooth, differentiable tension profiles.
AI.motivation: While cable tension determination is well-studied within the wrench-feasible workspace (WFW), few approaches address scenarios where CDPRs must operate outside this boundary, such as during aggressive maneuvers or cable failures. This limitation restricts the robots' capabilities in challenging operational conditions.
AI.method: The authors introduce an extended version of the Analytic Center method that: (1) determines cable tensions outside the WFW, (2) maintains differentiability, (3) includes non-linear constraints, (4) preserves continuous and differentiable tension profiles, (5) ensures fast real-time convergence to a unique solution, and (6) relegates wrench errors to a negligible area of the WFW.
AI.result: The proposed method demonstrates: (1) continuous and differentiable tension profiles, (2) fast real-time convergence to a unique solution, (3) superior smoothness and wrench error compared to other slack-based formulations, and (4) Pareto dominance over the leading state-of-the-art method. Effectiveness is validated through numerical experiments.
AI.conclusion: The extended Analytic Center method provides a practical solution for enabling CDPRs to operate beyond their WFW, with significant advantages in smoothness and error minimization. This enables safer and more capable operation during aggressive maneuvers and cable failure scenarios.

title: TFP: Temporally Conditioned Memory-Fusion Policies for Visuomotor Learning
comment: Accepted to the SemRob 2026 Workshop at Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS 2026)
summary: Vision--Language--Action (VLA) policies such as $π_{0.5}$ and OpenVLA perform well on many manipulation tasks, but they are often reactive: the next action is predicted from the current observation, instruction, and proprioceptive state. This assumption breaks down in stage-dependent manipulation, where visually similar states may require different actions depending on latent task progress and previous interaction outcomes. We argue that such tasks require not only memory, but dynamics-aware belief updates: the policy should preserve task progress during stable or occluded phases and revise its belief near contact, release, or subgoal transitions. We introduce Temporally Conditioned Memory-Fusion Policies (TFP), a lightweight memory-action framework for VLA backbones. TFP maintains an episode-local task-progress belief with Liquid Time-Constant dynamics and injects the updated belief directly into the flow-matching action decoder through adaptive modulation. This lets temporally accumulated context shape the generated action chunk, rather than serving only as passive history context. With a 3.3B-parameter model, TFP improves the average success rate from \(96.9\%\) to \(98.75\%\) on LIBERO and from \(91.4\%\) to \(93.77\%\) on LIBERO-plus. On the memory-focused MIKASA ShellGameTouch diagnostic, TFP achieves success up to \(75.0\%\). Mechanistic analyses show that write-gain changes near manipulation events are about \(6\times\) larger than far non-event phases, and hidden-state interventions show that the belief causally modulates generated action chunks. These results suggest that compact, event-sensitive memory dynamics can improve VLA policies under occlusion, visual perturbation, and stage-dependent task structure.

AI.tldr: TFP introduces event-aware memory dynamics to VLA policies, enabling them to preserve task progress and adapt beliefs during occluded or stage-dependent manipulation phases, improving success rates on LIBERO tasks by ~2% and achieving 75% on ShellGameTouch.
AI.motivation: VLA policies like π₀.₅ and OpenVLA are reactive (action from current observation only), which breaks down in stage-dependent manipulation where visually similar states require different actions based on task progress and interaction outcomes. Tasks require not just memory, but dynamics-aware belief updates that preserve task progress during stable/occluded phases and revise beliefs near contact/release/subgoal transitions.
AI.method: TFP is a lightweight memory-action framework for VLA backbones that maintains an episode-local task-progress belief using Liquid Time-Constant dynamics and injects the updated belief into a flow-matching action decoder via adaptive modulation, allowing temporally accumulated context to shape action chunks rather than serving only as passive history.
AI.result: With a 3.3B-parameter model, TFP improves LIBERO success from 96.9% to 98.75% and LIBERO-plus from 91.4% to 93.77%, achieves 75% success on MIKASA ShellGameTouch, and shows write-gain changes near manipulation events are ~6× larger than non-event phases, with hidden-state interventions confirming belief causally modulates action chunks.
AI.conclusion: Compact, event-sensitive memory dynamics can significantly improve VLA policies under occlusion, visual perturbation, and stage-dependent task structure by enabling temporally conditioned belief updates that adapt to manipulation events rather than just reactive current observations.

title: AnyDexRT: Calibration-Free Dexterous Hand Retargeting with Few-Shot Human Guidance
summary: Teleoperation is a key interface for controlling dexterous robotic hands and collecting demonstrations for imitation learning. Its effectiveness largely depends on kinematic retargeting, which maps operator hand motions to feasible and intuitive robot hand motions. Existing methods often require hand-crafted objectives, precise calibration, or global shape matching between human and robot hand spaces, making them sensitive to hand-specific tuning and less reliable across different dexterous hands. We propose AnyDexRT, a calibration-free retargeting method for intuitive dexterous teleoperation across human-like dexterous hands. AnyDexRT combines self-supervised fingertip correspondence learning with few-shot human guidance to anchor the mapping in task-relevant regions, and further refines pinch-related poses using a contact classifier. Experiments on diverse dexterous hands and real-world teleoperation tasks show that AnyDexRT improves retargeting quality, reduces manual tuning, and provides more intuitive and efficient control than prior retargeting methods. Project website: https://chenxi-wang.github.io/projects/anydexrt

AI.tldr: AnyDexRT is a calibration-free retargeting method for intuitive dexterous teleoperation across different human-like robotic hands, combining self-supervised fingertip correspondence learning with few-shot human guidance and a contact classifier.
AI.motivation: Teleoperation is critical for controlling dexterous robotic hands and collecting demonstrations for imitation learning. Existing retargeting methods require hand-crafted objectives, precise calibration, or global shape matching, making them sensitive to hand-specific tuning and less reliable across different dexterous hands.
AI.method: AnyDexRT integrates three key components: (1) self-supervised fingertip correspondence learning, (2) few-shot human guidance to anchor mappings in task-relevant regions, and (3) a contact classifier to refine pinch-related poses.
AI.result: Experiments across diverse dexterous hands and real-world teleoperation tasks demonstrate that AnyDexRT improves retargeting quality, significantly reduces manual tuning requirements, and provides more intuitive and efficient control compared to prior retargeting methods.
AI.conclusion: AnyDexRT enables calibration-free, intuitive dexterous teleoperation across different robotic hand types with minimal manual tuning, making it a more reliable and adaptable solution for practical applications.

title: SkillPlug: Unsupervised Skill Mining for Few-Shot Adaptation in Robotic Manipulation
summary: Learning transferable visuomotor imitation policies that generalize across diverse manipulation tasks and adapt rapidly to new tasks from only a handful of demonstrations remains challenging. Most modern policies are trained end-to-end to map observations directly to low-level actions, offering little explicit structure for reusing and recombining behaviors across tasks and making transfer data-inefficient under limited supervision. We propose SkillPlug, a plug-in framework that augments an existing visuomotor policy with a skill-conditioning module and mines a shared, transferable skill library from raw multi-task demonstrations. SkillPlug learns skills via self-supervised objectives that promote compact, reusable, and non-redundant behavior-level primitives, forming a task-shared prior for compositional control. After skill mining, we keep the learned skills fixed and specialize to unseen tasks by fine-tuning only lightweight router and action head, enabling efficient adaptation without full end-to-end retraining. We evaluate SkillPlug on two simulation benchmarks and on a real robot, and observe that the mined transferable skills consistently improve both multi-task performance and few-shot adaptation. Overall, SkillPlug offers a scalable way to mine reusable skills that improve data-efficient generalization in robotic manipulation.

AI.tldr: SkillPlug is a plug-in framework that augments existing visuomotor policies with skill-conditioning modules and mines transferable behavior primitives from multi-task demonstrations. It enables data-efficient generalization and rapid adaptation to new tasks by fine-tuning only lightweight components while keeping learned skills fixed.
AI.motivation: Learning transferable visuomotor policies that generalize across diverse tasks and adapt from few demonstrations is challenging. Existing end-to-end policies are data-inefficient under limited supervision and lack explicit structure for reusing and recombining behaviors across tasks.
AI.method: SkillPlug adds a skill-conditioning module to existing policies and mines a shared skill library from raw multi-task demonstrations via self-supervised objectives. It promotes compact, reusable, and non-redundant behavior-level primitives. After skill mining, it specializes to unseen tasks by fine-tuning only lightweight router and action head components while keeping learned skills fixed.
AI.result: Evaluated on two simulation benchmarks and a real robot, SkillPlug shows consistent improvement in both multi-task performance and few-shot adaptation compared to baseline approaches.
AI.conclusion: SkillPlug provides a scalable approach to mine reusable skills that enhance data-efficient generalization in robotic manipulation, enabling efficient adaptation without full end-to-end retraining.

title: FSD-VLN: Fast-Slow Dual-System Modeling for Aerial Long-Horizon Vision-Language Navigation
summary: Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) enables UAV autonomous navigation in unknown environments by mapping language instructions to real-time visual inputs. Compared with GPS-dependent or pre-programmed navigation, VLN supports intuitive human-machine interaction and stronger environmental adaptability, requiring tight integration of high-level semantic reasoning and low-latency flight control.Existing methods suffer from structural misalignment between global multimodal understanding and sequential action generation, causing jittery trajectories and severe decision latency for long-horizon aerial navigation. To solve this issue, we propose FSD-VLN, a fast-slow dual-system architecture disentangling semantic reasoning and low-latency flight command generation.The framework has two asynchronous branches: a slow stream extracting stable semantic priors from pre-trained vision-language models, and a Diffusion Transformer (DiT) fast stream modeling cross-temporal action distributions to produce consistent flight outputs. We further introduce a time-aware adaptive optimizer to stabilize long-sequence training and reduce gradient oscillation.Large-scale low-altitude simulation experiments show FSD-VLN achieves up to 2X higher navigation success rates on unseen scenes than SOTA methods, while cutting single-action inference delay and total task runtime by over 50%. Our work validates the benefit of decoupled semantic-control modeling and provides a practical paradigm for long-horizon aerial VLN.

AI.tldr: FSD-VLN is a fast-slow dual-system architecture for UAV Vision-Language Navigation that decouples semantic reasoning and low-latency flight command generation, achieving 2X higher navigation success rates on unseen scenes and cutting inference delay and runtime by over 50%.
AI.motivation: Existing VLN methods suffer from structural misalignment between global multimodal understanding and sequential action generation, causing jittery trajectories and severe decision latency for long-horizon aerial navigation. VLN requires tight integration of high-level semantic reasoning and low-latency flight control.
AI.method: FSD-VLN proposes a fast-slow dual-system architecture with two asynchronous branches: (1) a slow stream extracting stable semantic priors from pre-trained vision-language models, and (2) a Diffusion Transformer (DiT) fast stream modeling cross-temporal action distributions to produce consistent flight outputs. A time-aware adaptive optimizer is introduced to stabilize long-sequence training and reduce gradient oscillation.
AI.result: Large-scale low-altitude simulation experiments demonstrate that FSD-VLN achieves up to 2X higher navigation success rates on unseen scenes compared to SOTA methods, while cutting single-action inference delay by over 50% and total task runtime by more than 50%.
AI.conclusion: This work validates the benefit of decoupled semantic-control modeling and provides a practical paradigm for long-horizon aerial Vision-Language Navigation.

title: On Exploring Input Resolution Scaling For Anytime LiDAR Object Detection
summary: Making tradeoffs between execution latency and result utility (i.e., anytime computing) for adapting to dynamic operational requirements has been shown to enhance the performance of cyber-physical systems. In this work, we focus on enabling anytime computing for deep neural networks (DNNs) that process LiDAR point clouds for 3D object detection. We propose a novel method that enables multi-resolution inference for models that process point clouds as pillars or voxels, allowing the input to be dynamically scaled and processed at the resolution needed to meet timing requirements. Importantly, our memory-efficient approach requires the deployment of only a single DNN model, avoiding the need to deploy multiple models, each trained for a different input resolution. We also introduce a deadline-aware scheduler that selects the highest possible resolution for any given input by accurately predicting the execution time for all possible resolutions at runtime, which is challenging due to the irregularity of LiDAR point clouds. Experimental results on the nuScenes autonomous driving dataset demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing anytime computing approaches for LiDAR object detection. Finally, we deploy our approach in a simulated autonomous driving system, where it consistently enables collision-free navigation while avoiding unnecessary stalls caused by environmental complexity.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a multi-resolution inference method with a deadline-aware scheduler to enable anytime computing for DNN-based 3D object detection on LiDAR point clouds, using only a single model deployment.
AI.motivation: Tradeoffs between execution latency and result utility (anytime computing) enhance performance of cyber-physical systems, particularly for dynamic operational requirements in LiDAR-based 3D object detection.
AI.method: Multi-resolution inference for point cloud models (pillars or voxels) with dynamic input scaling; memory-efficient single-model deployment; deadline-aware scheduler that predicts execution time for all possible resolutions at runtime to handle LiDAR irregularity.
AI.result: Significantly outperforms existing anytime computing approaches on nuScenes dataset; enables collision-free navigation in simulated autonomous driving while avoiding stalls from environmental complexity.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method effectively enables anytime computing for LiDAR-based 3D object detection, balancing latency and utility through intelligent resolution selection and execution time prediction.

title: EgoWAM: World Action Models Beyond Pixels with In-the-Wild Egocentric Human Data
summary: Egocentric human data offers scalable supervision for robot manipulation. However, behavior cloning entangles transferable content like objects, scenes, and task semantics, with non-transferable factors like human morphology, head motion, and behavioral style. We study whether World Action Models (WAMs) provide a better training signal by requiring policies to predict not only actions, but also how the scene evolves. The central question is what world representation best enables human-to-robot transfer. We hypothesize that an effective world target should abstract appearance, capture agent-invariant physical effects, and separate camera motion from environment change. We introduce EgoWAM, a controlled human-robot co-training framework that fixes the policy backbone, action head, and data mixture while varying only the world prediction target, comparing Pixel, DINO, and 3D motion flow. Across three real-world bimanual tasks, WAM co-training scales more effectively with in-the-wild egocentric human data than behavior cloning. Pixel-based prediction transfers weakly, while DINO and 3D flow yield substantial gains: DINO improves out-of-distribution object and scene generalization by up to 4x, and 3D flow improves in-domain performance by 20-30%. More details: https://gatech-rl2.github.io/egowam.github.io

AI.tldr: This paper introduces EgoWAM, a framework for training robot manipulation policies from egocentric human data using World Action Models (WAMs) that predict scene evolution alongside actions. It compares Pixel, DINO, and 3D motion flow as world representations, finding that DINO and 3D flow significantly outperform behavior cloning and Pixel-based approaches.
AI.motivation: Behavior cloning from egocentric human data is challenging because it entangles transferable content (objects, scenes, task semantics) with non-transferable factors (human morphology, head motion, behavioral style). The authors aim to understand what world representation best enables effective human-to-robot transfer, hypothesizing that an effective world target should abstract appearance, capture agent-invariant physical effects, and separate camera motion from environment change.
AI.method: The researchers introduce EgoWAM, a controlled human-robot co-training framework that fixes the policy backbone, action head, and data mixture while varying only the world prediction target. They compare three world representations: Pixel-based prediction, DINO (a self-supervised vision transformer), and 3D motion flow. The framework is evaluated across three real-world bimanual tasks using in-the-wild egocentric human data.
AI.result: WAM co-training scales more effectively with egocentric human data than behavior cloning. Pixel-based prediction transfers weakly, while DINO and 3D flow yield substantial gains: DINO improves out-of-distribution object and scene generalization by up to 4x, and 3D flow improves in-domain performance by 20-30%.
AI.conclusion: The findings demonstrate that incorporating scene evolution prediction (World Action Models) significantly enhances robot manipulation learning from human demonstrations. Both DINO and 3D flow representations provide effective training signals that separate transferable content from non-transferable factors, making human-to-robot transfer more scalable and robust.

title: Harness VLA: Steering Frozen VLAs into Reliable Manipulation Primitives via Memory-Guided Agents
summary: Language-conditioned manipulation requires both precise contact-rich control and robust reasoning over language, scenes, and long horizons. End-to-end Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models provide strong local visuomotor skills, but they are trained on in-distribution task trajectories and often fail under deployment perturbations such as semantic retargeting, goal re-binding, spatial-layout shifts, and unstable local contacts. LLM coding agents provide complementary semantic and compositional reasoning, but purely analytic primitives struggle with irregular grasping, constrained placement, and articulated-object interaction. We present Harness VLA, a memory-augmented agentic framework that exposes a frozen VLA as a retryable contact-rich primitive and composes it with a small fixed library of analytic primitives for grounding, staging, transport, navigation, and release. Rather than expanding the skill library, the harness learns the operating range of these fixed primitives from task-specific execution traces, global success rules, and failure models. By lifting semantic re-grounding, non-contact execution, and VLA re-staging to the planner while reserving the frozen VLA for local contact-rich phases, Harness VLA extends pretrained VLAs beyond their original trajectory distribution without finetuning. Across perturbed tabletop, household kitchen, and clean-to-randomized bimanual manipulation, Harness VLA improves over the strongest relevant baselines by 38.6 and 25.4 percentage points on LIBERO-Pro and RoboCasa365, respectively, and reaches 58.4% on RoboTwin C2R.

AI.tldr: Harness VLA is a memory-augmented framework that combines a frozen VLA model with analytic primitives to extend pretrained VLA capabilities beyond their original training distribution for robust language-conditioned manipulation.
AI.motivation: Language-conditioned manipulation requires precise contact-rich control and robust reasoning over language, scenes, and long horizons. Current approaches have limitations: end-to-end VLA models fail under deployment perturbations (semantic retargeting, goal re-binding, spatial-layout shifts, unstable local contacts), while LLM coding agents provide semantic reasoning but struggle with irregular grasping, constrained placement, and articulated-object interaction.
AI.method: Harness VLA exposes a frozen VLA as a retryable contact-rich primitive composed with a small fixed library of analytic primitives for grounding, staging, transport, navigation, and release. The framework learns operating ranges from execution traces, success rules, and failure models. It lifts semantic re-grounding, non-contact execution, and VLA re-staging to the planner while reserving the frozen VLA for local contact-rich phases, extending pretrained VLAs without finetuning.
AI.result: Across perturbed tabletop, household kitchen, and clean-to-randomized bimanual manipulation, Harness VLA improves over baselines by 38.6 percentage points on LIBERO-Pro and 25.4 percentage points on RoboCasa365, reaching 58.4% on RoboTwin C2R.
AI.conclusion: By composing frozen VLA models with analytic primitives and handling semantic re-grounding at the planner level, Harness VLA successfully extends pretrained VLAs beyond their original trajectory distribution, achieving significant performance improvements across multiple benchmarks without requiring finetuning.

title: FabriVLA: A Lightweight Vision-Language-Action Model for Precise Multi-Task Manipulation
summary: We present FabriVLA, a lightweight Vision-Language-Action model for Precise Multi-Task Manipulation. FabriVLA combines an InternVL3.5 vision-language backbone with a flow-matching action head featuring gated self-attention across action tokens and shallow VLM layer fusion for enriched spatial context. The model is trained via single stage joint optimization from a pretrained VLM and randomly initialized action head. On the Meta-World MT50 benchmark spanning 50 diverse manipulation tasks, FabriVLA achieves a tier-average success rate of 90.0%, demonstrating that a compact VLA built on a 1B scale VLM can achieve strong performance without relying on multi billion parameter VLA backbones.
